title: Adaptive KV Eviction Economics: Product Brief & Ops Playbook
author: Priya Kumar
content:
Overview:

This document describes the Adaptive KV Eviction Economics initiative: a product and operational playbook to coordinate key-value (KV) cache eviction and retention policies across model variants, tenants, and runtime topologies to reduce end-to-end token cost while preserving latency SLOs and inference quality. It combines a product brief, minimum viable requirements (PRD), high-level design, rollout roadmap, pricing/packaging implications, release notes, and runbook tasks for post-launch operations.

Goals and thesis:

- Reduce average token compute cost attributable to redundant KV cache loads by 12–30% for multi-variant serving workloads.
- Preserve 95th percentile latency SLOs for conversational flows (target: p95 <= configured latency tier).
- Provide transparent billing signals and crediting for KV hits to enable commercial packaging (e.g., KV-hit discounts).
- Make eviction policies configurable per-tenant and autopilot-tunable per-workload.

Scope (what's in/out):

In scope:
- Adaptive eviction policies implemented in the serving runtime and exposed via per-tenant policy objects.
- A cost-aware eviction algorithm combining recency, frequency, and estimated token-cost-savings signal.
- Console UX for policy selection and per-route policy overrides.
- Telemetry and observability (per-tenant KV hit rate, estimated token-savings, policy regressions).
- Billing/credit schema proposals for KV credits and KV-hit discounts.

Out of scope (phase 1):
- On-prem appliance integration changes beyond policy config API.
- Deep model-level cache insertion hooks (future phase).

Success metrics (first 6 months):

- System metric: Mean per-token compute cost drop attributable to KV coordination >= 15% for pilot tenants.
- Performance metric: No more than 2% regression in generation quality (measured by eval prompt set).
- Reliability metric: Incidents attributable to KV eviction policy changes <= 1 per quarter for pilot tenants.
- Adoption metric: 25% of enterprise pilot tenants adopt adaptive policies within 3 months.

User stories / primary personas:

- As an ML platform engineer, I want a default cost-aware eviction policy so my tenant reduces token spend without manual tuning.
- As a product owner, I want per-route overrides so critical flows keep longer KV retention.
- As a billing analyst, I want KV-hit telemetry correlated with billing so I can validate KV credit allocations.

PRD: Requirements (MUST/SHOULD/CAN)

| ID | Priority | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|-----|----------|-------------|--------------------|
| R1 | MUST | Runtime supports pluggable eviction module with three built-in policies: LRU, LFU, Cost-Aware TTL | Unit tests, runtime flag to switch policy per-pool and per-tenant, integration test validating eviction outcome on synthetic workloads |
| R2 | MUST | Expose policy object via Control Plane API and Console with schema (ttl, max_entries, cost_prefactor, override_rules) | API docs + example payloads; Console form with validation; e2e apply test |
| R3 | MUST | Emit telemetry: kv.hit_rate, kv.eviction_count, kv.estimated_token_savings (per-route, per-tenant) | Metrics appear in telemetry pipeline; dashboards defined; alerts for sudden drops in hit_rate |
| R4 | SHOULD | Autosuggest policy adjustments based on historical traffic and model variants | MVP: nightly suggestions; UI shows expected savings and confidence score |
| R5 | SHOULD | Billing layer records KV-hit credits for eligible requests | Prototype costing calculation available and validated with finance team |
| R6 | CAN | Provide SDK helpers for local dev (simulating eviction behavior) | Developer docs and small Python helper library |

High-level design

1) Components:
- Control Plane policy store: canonical policy objects per-tenant/route.
- Serving runtime eviction module: pluggable with a Cost-Aware policy.
- Telemetry pipeline: enriched metrics and event tagging.
- Console & API UX: policy editing, suggestions, and rollout controls.
- Billing bridge: computes KV-hit credits and exposes to billing downstream.

2) Cost-Aware eviction algorithm (overview):
- Score each cache entry = alpha * recency_score + beta * frequency_score + gamma * token_cost_savings_estimate.
- token_cost_savings_estimate = expected_future_token_count_saved * model_unit_cost.
- Evict entries with lowest score when capacity exceeded.
- alpha/beta/gamma are tenant-configurable; autosuggest uses historical tracebacks to tune gamma per-variant.

3) Data needed for scoring:
- Per-entry last_access_ts, access_count, average_future_prefix_length (estimated via historical patterns), model_variant_cost_profile.

4) API contract (example):
- PATCH /v1/tenants/{t}/kv-policy
- Payload fields: ttl_seconds, max_entries, policy_type (lru|lfu|cost-aware), cost_prefactor, rules[{route_regex, min_ttl, priority}]

Example payload:
```json
{
  "policy_type": "cost-aware",
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "max_entries": 50000,
  "cost_prefactor": 1.2,
  "rules": [
    { "route_regex": "/v1/chat/agent/.*", "min_ttl": 7200, "priority": 1 }
  ]
}
```

Operational considerations & SLOs

- SLOs:
  - KV pipeline availability: 99.95% monthly.
  - KV-hit telemetry freshness: 30s (90th percentile).
  - p95 inference latency impact after policy change: < +5% compared to baseline.

- Alerts to create:
  - kv.hit_rate drops > 40% for a high-volume tenant within 10 minutes.
  - estimated_token_savings > 2x historical baseline (possible regression in measurement).
  - policy enforcement errors > 1% of requests for a tenant.

- Runbook excerpt (for oncall):
  1. If kv.hit_rate alert fires, identify tenant and recent policy changes.
  2. Rollback tenant policy to previous version via Control Plane API.
  3. If rollback fails, change policy_type to LRU as emergency safe mode.
  4. Notify product and ML teams; run lightweight traffic replay to validate behavior.

Rollout plan & roadmap (quarters)

- Q2 2026: Design, runtime hooks, and API schema; limited unit tests and local dev helpers.
- Q3 2026: Implement LRU/LFU + Cost-Aware prototype; internal dogfood with 3 pilot tenants; initial telemetry dashboards.
- Q4 2026: Console UX, autosuggest MVP, and billing bridge prototype (KV-hit credits).
- Q1 2027: Wider beta, finance validation for KV credits, per-route override polish.
- Q2 2027: General availability with multi-tenant autoscaling constraints and enterprise config controls.

Pricing & packaging implications

- KV-hit credits model (proposal):
  - Define a KV-hit as a cache hit that avoids > X tokens of compute (threshold tunable).
  - KV-hit credit = unit_price_per_token_saved * estimated_tokens_saved * credit_factor.
  - Packaging: include a baseline KV-credit allowance for enterprise Dedicated plans; additional KV-credits purchasable as add-on.

- Commercial impacts to validate with Finance & Sales:
  - How to audit and dispute KV-hit counts.
  - How credits affect refunding and overage calculations.
  - Competitive messaging and support for customers migrating from flat per-token billing.

Release notes (candidate language for product announcements)

Title: Adaptive KV Eviction — Cost-aware cache policies and billing preview\nSummary: Introduces tenant-level adaptive KV eviction policies that reduce token compute spend by prioritizing entries that save the most future compute. Includes API, console controls, telemetry, and a billing preview that implements KV-hit crediting for eligible workloads. Pilot customers can opt in via the Console.

Operational checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] End-to-end integration tests for policy enforcement.
- [ ] Dashboards and alerting configured for pilot tenants.
- [ ] Billing bridge dry-run with finance team on sample data.
- [ ] Documentation for console UX and API examples.
- [ ] Oncall runbook published and reviewed.

Risks & mitigations

- Risk: Inaccurate token-savings estimates cause wrong eviction decisions and quality regressions.
  - Mitigation: Conservative default gamma; safety override rules (per-route min_ttl) and canary traffic before tenant-wide rollout.
- Risk: Billing disputes over KV credit attribution.
  - Mitigation: Add deterministic event logs for each KV decision and store a 30-day audit window; provide CSV exports for customers.
- Risk: Increased memory pressure leading to node OOMs under misconfigured max_entries.
  - Mitigation: Default global capping per-pool and hard safety guardrails in the runtime.

Appendix A — Example dashboard panels

- Tenant KV hit rate (1m/5m/30m)
- Estimated token savings (rolling 24h)
- Policy change timeline with diff view
- Per-route hit-rate and p95 latency correlation

Appendix B — Example config matrix (recommended defaults)

| Tenant size | max_entries | ttl_seconds | policy_type | cost_prefactor |
|-------------|-------------:|------------:|-------------|----------------:|
| Small / dev | 5,000 | 600 | lru | 0.8 |
| Mid | 50,000 | 3600 | cost-aware | 1.0 |
| Large / enterprise | 250,000 | 7200 | cost-aware | 1.4 |

Appendix C — Sample troubleshooting CLI commands

- View tenant policy: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{id}/kv-policy
- Rollback policy: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{id}/kv-policy/rollback -d '{"version":"v2026-09-12"}'
- Force safe-mode (LRU): curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{id}/kv-policy -d '{"policy_type":"lru"}'

Notes & next steps:

- Phase 2 ideas: cross-variant shared KV indexing, model-insert hints, and probabilistic early-eviction for low-confidence entries.
- Coordinate with Private deployment team for required runtime flags and packaging changes.

End of document.
